Subject: Recap & POC plan — model selection + next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed POC plan so we can lock timelines:

Recap of needs (from our notes):
- Primary use case: product help/FAQ + short summarization of policy updates across internal docs.
- Expected traffic pattern: bursty during business hours; latency-sensitive for UI snippets.
- Multilingual: English primary, Spanish as secondary (some French later).
- Success criteria: answer accuracy on curated QA set, hallucination rate < 5% on domain queries, p95 latency <= 250ms for single-turn UI calls, and acceptable cost per 1k tokens for long-running summarization flows.

Proposed POC (6 weeks):
1) Kickoff (week 0): share sample dataset & SLOs — Sam/Ju lia provide ~200 labeled QA pairs + 50 doc excerpts (Sam: can you confirm delivery by Tue?)
2) Week 1: Baseline run — Aditya will run 3 candidate open models on a dev split (details below) and report accuracy/latency/cost.
3) Week 2–3: Model tuning and eval harness — automated evaluation on larger prompt set; human spot checks for hallucination.
4) Week 4: User testing with UI integration (short path) — latency tests and fallback behavior.
5) Week 5: Final report + decision and recommend production config (model, quantization, routing policy).

Model selection (initial recommendation):
- Primary candidate: Llama-2-13b-chat (4-bit quantized) — good balance of quality and latency for enterprise text QA and multilingual capability.
- Fallback (low-latency path): Llama-2-7b-chat (4-bit) — use for UI real-time snippets where p95 matters.
- Multilingual note: we’ll evaluate Spanish prompts across both candidates; if quality gaps appear, we may try a 13B multilingual-optimized variant or apply retrieval augmentation.

Technical / success ownership:
- Acme: provide samples, labeled QA pairs, and acceptance criteria sign-off.
- Redwood (Aditya): run evaluations, provision POC infra, surface latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Redwood (Marissa): project lead and commercial contact; coordinate procurement and SOW.

Attachments: Acme-POC-Scope-v1.docx (draft scope), sample_prompts.csv (please fill any missing labels).

Next steps:
- Sam: confirm dataset delivery by Tue 30 Jun and confirm Julia (procurement) to loop in for any SOW/procurement questions.
- Aditya/Dev: confirm technical feasibility and any compliance questions in reply.
- I'll schedule a 30m kickoff for Wed (options: 7/1 9:30am PT or 7/2 11:00am PT).

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Sam / Marissa —

Quick technical follow-up on model selection and the automatic fallback behavior:

Fallback routing: we can implement an automated routing policy that prefers the 13B candidate by default and falls back to 7B when (a) observed p95 latency for a route exceeds a configured threshold OR (b) if the request is flagged as non-critical (UI hint). We can also scope deterministic routing per route (i.e., some endpoints always use 7B). We’ll provide a routing policy config you can edit.

Quantization and expected latency: with 4-bit quantization and our optimized kernels, initial p95 estimates for single-turn QA on a 13B model in our Dedicated POC environment are ~180–300ms depending on sequence length; 7B is typically ~90–140ms. We'll benchmark on your actual sample prompts and report back.

Multilingual evaluation: please include Spanish variants of the QA pairs where available. If you don’t have Spanish labels we can do synthetic translation for initial checks but recommend human-labeled Spanish examples for production decisions.

Dataset ask: for the evaluation harness, aim for:
- 200–500 QA pairs total (split 70/30 dev/test)
- 20–30 longer summarization examples (300–1,000 tokens)

Ballpark cost for POC infra (compute + usage): expect $3k–$8k depending on run intensity and model choice — we’ll provide a more precise estimate after the first baseline run.

I’ll take the 7/2 11:00am PT kickoff and will prepare the baseline checklist and a small test harness.
